reason: The AD Connector compatibility list states AD Connector can authenticate console users with their AD credentials without setting up SAML infrastructure.

The context on the AD Connector compatibility page states EC2 Windows or Linux seamless domain join joins the self-managed AD and the joined instance communicates directly with AD and bypasses AD Connector.
The FAQ quote states AD Connector is a directory gateway that redirects requests to on-premises AD without caching any information in the cloud.

The two quotes state AD Connector is a proxy connecting WorkSpaces, Quick and EC2 Windows Server to on-premises AD and that it forwards sign-in requests to the on-premises domain controllers for authentication.
Under AD Connector prerequisites the quotes require at least two subnets in different Availability Zones and a VPC connected to the existing network through VPN or Direct Connect.
The quote states all directory data remains on your domain controllers and Directory Service does not replicate any of it.
The quotes state AD Connector eliminates directory synchronization and hosting a federation infrastructure, and that you keep managing users, groups and passwords with standard on-premises AD tools.
The quote states no transitive trust support, a 1-to-1 relationship, and a unique AD Connector per on-premises domain including child domains.
The quote under the AD Connector tab states AD Connector is not compatible with RDS SQL Server.
The note states AD Connector cannot be shared with other accounts (suggesting Managed Microsoft AD sharing) and is not multi-VPC aware, so WorkSpaces must be in the same VPC.
The quote gives the two sizes with their intended operation rates, spreading load across multiple connectors, and no enforced user or connection limits.
The When to use quote states AD Connector is your best choice to use an existing on-premises directory with compatible AWS services.
The quotes support the Oct 2, 2025 API-driven Standard to Enterprise upgrade without support tickets, but the condition 'console support came later' is not stated anywhere in the quotes or context.
The document history row dated July 30, 2025 states Hybrid Edition connects your self-managed AD with AWS Managed Microsoft AD.

The quotes support the Apr 1, 2026 date, the opt-in Region scope with the UAE and Bahrain exceptions and the hourly plus data transfer cost, but the scope qualifier 'Enterprise Edition' is not stated in the quotes or context.
The document history row dated March 31, 2023 states the guide added content about AWS PrivateLink.
The Aug 15, 2025 post states Standard Edition sharing went from 5 to 25 accounts and Enterprise from 125 to 500 accounts.
The history row dated June 30, 2026 states Simple AD closes to new customers starting July 30, 2026 and existing customers retain full functionality.
The history row dated July 30, 2026 states Simple AD is no longer open to new customers.
The quotes state directory members have no AWS access by default, IAM roles are assigned to give access, and the directory must have an access URL before console access is granted.

The FAQ quotes state IAM roles can be assigned to Managed Microsoft AD, Simple AD, and on-premises AD (via AD Connector) users and groups, with a customer-specific console URL for corporate credentials.
The decision guide table row maps 'Run Active Directory dependent workloads in AWS' to AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
The decision guide table row maps joining AWS workloads to on-premises AD Domain Services to AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
The quotes describe a highly available, fully managed AD that extends on-premises AD configurations and can domain-join EC2, WorkSpaces and RDS for SQL Server.
The limitations list states no revert, no restore from earlier snapshots, four to five hours, and additional cost.
The use case page states trusts connect Managed Microsoft AD to existing AD without synchronizing users, groups or passwords, and that migration can use ADMT with PES.

The pricing quotes state 1,500 domain controller hours across all managed directories in the first 30 days and that directory sharing does not qualify; the context also excludes multi-Region data transfer.
The FSx guide gives the two options (Managed Microsoft AD or self-managed AD) and states FSx does not support AD Connector or Simple AD.
The FAQ quote states Hybrid Edition extends existing AD without fully migrating, its domain controllers join the existing forest, and AD data replicates into AWS.
The quote states it is powered by an actual Windows Server AD managed by AWS and enables migrating a broad range of AD-aware applications.

The quotes and their context list the Admin account's OU actions (users, groups, computers, group policies, OUs) and domain-wide DNS and log rights, and state it lacks permissions outside its OU such as the parent OU.
The quotes state compatibility with multiple AWS services and third-party applications and that AWS cannot guarantee any application is or will continue to be compatible.
The quote states AWS provides monitoring, daily snapshots and recovery while you add users and groups and administer Group Policy with familiar AD tools on a domain-joined Windows computer.
The quote states Managed Microsoft AD alone enables console sign-in, and with IAM Identity Center adds short-term SDK and CLI credentials and preconfigured SAML integrations.
The FAQ quote states backups are taken automatically once per day and the EBS volumes are encrypted at rest.
The quote states a highly available pair of domain controllers across different Availability Zones with AWS managing monitoring, recovery, replication, snapshots and software updates.
The FAQ quote states you are assigned an OU and an administrative account with delegated administrative rights for the OU.
The quote states an ENI is created for each domain controller, is essential for connectivity, and should never be deleted.
The FAQ quote gives 17 GB for Enterprise and Hybrid Editions supporting up to 100,000 users or 500,000 objects, and the context says these numbers are an estimate.
The FAQ quote states failed domain controllers are replaced automatically in the same AZ with the same IP and full disaster recovery uses the latest backup.
